title: Agorapulse vs Hootsuite 2026: Which Wins (+ What Both Miss)
summary: Agorapulse vs Hootsuite in 2026: compare pricing tiers, listening depth, G2 ratings, and the video-era gap both scheduling tools miss before you pick one.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Agorapulse vs Hootsuite in 2026 comes down to who each tool actually fits: Agorapulse wins on price-to-seat value, G2 satisfaction, and native TikTok scheduling; Hootsuite wins on integration breadth and listening reach — though its deepest listening window is reserved for the Advanced tier and above. Neither tool, at any price, transcribes what a creator actually says in a video.


Compare the pricing pages alone and you'll get half the story. The cheaper-looking plan often hides the exact feature you signed up for two tiers up, and 2025-2026 brought structural changes to both vendors that most existing comparisons haven't caught up to yet.


Agorapulse spent 2025 acquiring a standalone social listening company, then spent early 2026 quietly retiring that company's own tools and repricing listening as a separate, expensive add-on. Hootsuite spent June 2026 rebuilding its entire product around four named apps and an AI agent, but its deepest listening window still sits behind the pricier tiers most teams skip. Pick a plan off last year's feature list and you end up paying for capability that isn't actually unlocked at your price point.


Below: a pricing breakdown, where each tool actually pulls ahead, where both fall short even at their most expensive tiers, and a framework to pick the right one for 2026.


## Agorapulse vs Hootsuite: At-a-Glance Comparison (2026 Pricing)

G2 ratings above are a September 2026 snapshot — review counts shift week to week, so treat them as directional rather than fixed. Both platforms include 10 social profiles at their entry tier before per-profile add-on fees kick in.


## Where Agorapulse Wins


Agorapulse wins on value density: it's the cheaper seat, the higher G2 score, and the platform that built TikTok scheduling into its core product rather than bolting it on.


**Three places Agorapulse pulls ahead:**


1.


**Price-to-seat value.** At every published tier, Agorapulse undercuts Hootsuite's equivalent plan — $79 vs $99 at entry, $119 vs $199 at mid-tier — while both cap out around 10 accounts before add-on fees (Source:[Agorapulse Pricing, 2026](https://www.agorapulse.com/pricing/) ;[Hootsuite Plans, 2026](https://www.hootsuite.com/plans) ).


2.


**G2 satisfaction.** Agorapulse holds a 4.5/5 rating against Hootsuite's 4.3/5 (as of September 2026), even with roughly an eighth of the review volume — Hootsuite's larger, longer-tenured install base pulls in more total reviews but not a higher average (Source:[G2 — Agorapulse](https://www.g2.com/sellers/agorapulse) ;[G2 — Hootsuite](https://www.g2.com/sellers/hootsuite) ).


3.


**Native TikTok workflow.** Agorapulse ships native TikTok auto-publish, a shared TikTok content calendar, comment-inbox management, and TikTok-inclusive Power Reports as first-class features, not an integration bolted on after the fact (Source:[Agorapulse — TikTok scheduling & management, 2026](https://www.agorapulse.com/tiktok-integration/) ). For what TikTok-native *listening* — not just scheduling — actually requires, see our[TikTok social listening guide](https://syncly.app/blog/tiktok-social-listening-guide) .


The catch sits underneath the pricing table. Agorapulse acquired Mention — a standalone listening vendor — in a deal announced in 2025, rebranding it "Mention by Agorapulse" (Source:[Agorapulse blog — Mention acquisition rationale](https://www.agorapulse.com/blog/agorapulse-news/mention-by-agorapulse-why-were-investing-in-social-listening/) ). Owning a listening company doesn't mean listening comes bundled: Mention's legacy self-serve tiers were discontinued in July 2025, and its own scheduling/inbox features (Publish/Respond) were retired entirely on January 30, 2026. What's left for new customers is a single $599/month "Company Plan" capped at five alerts — a separate purchase, not a plan upgrade (Source:[CheckThat.ai — Mention Pricing 2026](https://checkthat.ai/brands/mention/pricing) ). Reviewers also flag "expensive pricing" and "difficult reporting" repeatedly in aggregated G2 pros/cons, and approval workflows reportedly get clunky once client workspaces scale up (Source:[G2 Agorapulse reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/agorapulse/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) ).


## Where Hootsuite Wins


Hootsuite wins on two things Agorapulse can't currently match: how many other tools it plugs into, and how far its listening reaches once you're paying for the tier that unlocks it.


Hootsuite lists 103 integrations in its app directory — Slack, HubSpot, Canva, Salesforce, Dropbox, Google My Business — a broader documented ecosystem than Agorapulse's, whose own integration count isn't clearly published (Source:[GetApp — Hootsuite, 2026](https://www.getapp.com/marketing-software/a/hootsuite/) ;[SourceForge — Agorapulse integrations](https://sourceforge.net/software/product/AgoraPulse/integrations/) ).


The bigger story is June 2026's "Social OS" relaunch — a full architecture split into four named apps: Perch (publishing), Nest (customer care/community), Parliament (employee advocacy), and Lumen (social intelligence, Talkwalker-powered). Alongside it, Hootsuite introduced "Wisdom," an AI agent built on 15+ years of proprietary data and more than 150 million monitored sources, plus MCP connectors across the suite (Source:[Hootsuite Newsroom — Wisdom launch, June 2026](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/24/3316916/0/en/hootsuite-rebuilds-for-the-ai-era-introducing-wisdom-a-social-first-ai-agent-turning-social-signals-into-action.html) ).


**The tier gate matters here — but it's a sliding scale, not a hard wall.** Lumen's listening window scales with the plan: Standard is capped at a 7-day lookback, and the $399/month Advanced tier extends that to a 30-day window plus approval, routing, and collaboration controls. The full 150M+-source breadth Hootsuite advertises for Wisdom, along with enterprise governance and SSO, is reserved for the custom-priced Enterprise tier (Source:[Reputation Insider — Hootsuite/Lumen review, 2026](https://www.reputation-insider.com/hootsuite-review/) ). Wisdom/OwlyGPT AI, by contrast, spans tiers starting at Standard — a real edge over Agorapulse, which gates its own AI features to the contact-sales Custom tier. And Hootsuite bills per named seat from first login, so a five-person team pays for five seats even if only two log in daily — a pattern reviewers call out directly: one review calls the $99-per-seat price "tough to justify" for a small business on a tight budget (Source:[StartupOwl — Hootsuite Review 2026](https://startupowl.com/reviews/hootsuite) ).


## Where Both Fall Short: The Spoken-Word Gap


Neither platform hears what a creator actually says on camera — and that gap doesn't close no matter which tier you buy.


Agorapulse's real listening now lives in a $599/month bolt-on that inherited Mention's original architecture: keyword, hashtag, and caption matching. Hootsuite's Lumen, even with 150 million-plus indexed sources, works the same way — it's a text and metadata engine wearing a bigger dataset. Neither one transcribes audio or reads what's spoken inside a TikTok, Reel, or Short. A creator can talk through a 40-second review of your product, name it three times out loud, and never type the brand name anywhere in the caption or hashtags — and both platforms would show nothing.


**Spoken brand mentions** : references to a brand that occur only in a video's audio track or on-screen visuals — never typed as a caption, hashtag, or @-mention — and therefore invisible to any listening tool that indexes text rather than the content of the video itself.


This is the structural blind spot both vendors carry into 2026, regardless of pricing tier. ## How to Decide Between Agorapulse and Hootsuite in 2026


Three questions settle most of this faster than a feature-by-feature audit.


1.


**How many seats, and how is the team structured?** A small in-house team or an agency under ~10-15 client seats gets more from Agorapulse's per-seat economics and TikTok-native workflow — see our roundup of[listening tools for agencies](https://syncly.app/blog/best-social-listening-tools-for-marketing-agencies) if listening is part of that retainer. A larger org juggling many integrations and profiles tends to lean toward Hootsuite.


2.


**What's the actual budget for listening, not just scheduling?** If listening is a "nice to have," either tool's entry tier covers scheduling fine. If listening is the point, budget separately for Agorapulse's $599/month Mention add-on, or for Hootsuite's Advanced tier and up — neither vendor's entry-level Standard price includes meaningful listening depth. A dedicated[social listening platform](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) is worth pricing out on its own before you commit to either bolt-on.


3.


**Does your category live in spoken video content?** Beauty, F&B, fashion, and CPG brands run on conversations that happen inside video, not captions. If so, treat the scheduler choice and the listening choice as two separate purchases.


**Quick rule:** tight budget, small team, TikTok-first workflow → Agorapulse. Larger team, integration-heavy stack, willing to pay for Advanced-or-above listening → Hootsuite. Video-driven category either way → pair your pick with a dedicated video listening layer.


## Key Takeaways


-


**Agorapulse wins on value** — lower per-seat pricing, a 4.5/5 G2 score, and native TikTok scheduling — but its real listening now lives in a separate $599/mo "Mention by Agorapulse" plan, not its core tiers.


-


**Hootsuite wins on breadth** — 103 integrations and an AI agent (Wisdom) available from its Standard tier — but Lumen's listening window is tier-gated too: 7 days on Standard, 30 days on the $399/mo Advanced plan, and full 150M+-source breadth only at custom-priced Enterprise.


-


**Neither tool reads video natively.** Both remain caption, hashtag, and keyword-based for listening, even at their most expensive tiers.


-


**The advertised price rarely includes the listening depth vendors lead with in marketing.** Budget for the add-on or the upper tiers separately before comparing "starting prices."


-


**If your category runs on spoken video content** , the scheduler decision and the listening decision are two different purchases — plan for both.


## The 2026 Verdict


Agorapulse and Hootsuite are both competent schedulers solving a familiar problem well: queue posts, manage an inbox, keep a content calendar organized across profiles. Agorapulse does it cheaper with a G2 edge; Hootsuite does it with more integrations and a broader AI and listening push, if you're willing to pay up for the tiers that unlock the deeper end of it.


But the real 2026 question isn't which scheduler wins on price — it's that both vendors are still selling text-era listening dressed up in 2026 packaging, whether that's a $599 bolt-on or Enterprise-only listening breadth. If your brand lives in beauty, F&B, fashion, or CPG, the conversations that move purchase decisions are spoken, not typed, and neither tool is built to catch that at any price.
